item.title: security: Cybersecurity IR Workshop: The workshop you shouldn’t miss
item.description:
Microsoft Security promoted a cybersecurity incident response workshop focused on practical guidance from DART to improve preparedness and response. The post frames resilience as starting before an incident.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: github: Credential revocation and deauthorization by token type
item.description:
GitHub added self-service incident response actions to deauthorize and revoke user credentials by token type and by specific user. The update extends existing credential revocation workflows for security incidents.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: security: 128 Seconds to disruption: Microsoft Defender stops ransomware at QNET
item.description:
Microsoft Defender isolated a compromised QNET endpoint in 128 seconds, interrupting a multi-stage ransomware attack before the payload could persist or spread.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Real world incident response: Microsoft and AXA XL strengthen cyber resilience
item.description:
Microsoft and AXA XL are collaborating to give cyber insurance policyholders direct access to Microsoft Incident Response services. The goal is to help organizations coordinate technical response, business decisions, and insurance actions during incidents.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: github: Self-service credential revocation for incident response
item.description:
GitHub Enterprise owners can now use a new break-glass capability to immediately revoke all credentials for a compromised account or stolen credentials during incident response. The feature is self-service and intended for urgent security handling.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: security: One intrusion, two cyberattackers: Uncovering parallel threat activity
item.description:
Microsoft describes a ransomware case where two threat actors operated in parallel during the same intrusion, using overlapping tactics and evasion methods. The report emphasizes that isolated telemetry can miss complex attacks when activity from multiple actors is blended together.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Reconstructing AI activity in investigations
item.description:
Microsoft published a security playbook for investigating AI activity in Microsoft 365 Copilot and Azure AI services. It focuses on using telemetry to reconstruct events, assess data exposure, and speed up threat detection.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog
